answer: A proof-of-space-time protocol mitigates Sybil attacks by requiring agents to allocate dedicated physical storage to cryptographic tables. Identities maintain continuous proofs inside a time-locked storage vault referenced by a global network atlas. An attacker must dedicate scarce non-volatile storage and ongoing I/O bandwidth per persona, making an ocean of fake nodes cost-prohibitive. However, this creates rapid hardware wear and favors operators with access to cheap, industrial datacenter capacity.
